pattern.description: A job-status log updates live: the step label flips to 'Step 2/2: Transforming and loading', the progress bar restarts, and new log lines are inserted at the top of the status table, pushing earlier lines down.
pattern.why_premium: Real progress readouts (row counts, loader names) stream in while the narration says 'without any tedious data collection', so the automation is shown working rather than claimed.

build_hint.gsap: Timeline of discrete updates: tl.set('.step-label', {textContent: 'Step 2/2: Transforming and loading'}).fromTo('.progress-fill', {scaleX: 0}, {scaleX: 0.5, duration: 0.12, ease: 'none', transformOrigin: 'left'}, '<').add(() => prependLogRow(text)) with each new row using gsap.set (no tween) and the list shifting by one row height; spinner gsap.to('.spinner', {rotation: 360, repeat: -1, duration: 0.8, ease: 'none'}).
build_hint.remotion: Derive state from frame: step label and visible log rows switch at fixed frames (no interpolation); progress width = interpolate(frame, [0, 4], [0, 50], {extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}) percent; spinner rotate = (frame * 15) % 360 degrees, linear.

notes: Filmstrip thumbnails are cropped to a small strip, so the exact order of label swap, bar reset and row insertion is hard to read. ai_answer_stream is the nearest fit (log lines arriving one by one), but this is a job status log rather than an AI answer; a 'status log update' pattern might be worth considering. b01 text lists the log lines read from the end frame (OCR showed 'CCD5' for 'CCDS').
